content_of_post_to_comment: you matter, and yes, you really do. You could live for 3 more days or 90 more years, so every day, be grateful and don’t take it for granted. I made that mistake countless times. Spend time with loved ones, hug, kiss, laugh, have fun, and don’t give a f*** about what others think. Ask your crush out, travel, live life to the fullest, and be yourself. It doesn’t matter if you’re gay, bi, straight, Black, White, Asian, old, young, rich, poor, female, or male—at the end of the day, we’re human. Your chance of being born is 1 in 420 trillion; that’s an unbelievably high number, which you can’t even begin to imagine how large it is. You are so lucky to be here. I spent the last 6 years worrying, stressing every day about the future, and unfortunately, I still do. I have suffered from horrible depression, and some days I feel like giving up, but I remember this: 2026 so far has been poor but better and there is hope, and, to be honest—relationships, friends, personal life have been mixed great things and issues —but I keep on fighting. I know it’s hard, but no one deserves to feel like I do, and that’s why I’m commenting. I try to remain hopeful. I wish anyone seeing this comment the best in life and strength to overcome any issues. Be kind to everyone, smile at that one person, ask how they are, spread kindness and not hate. I really hope this helps someone reading this, and thank you for taking your time to read.
comment: The part about spending years worrying about the future hit close to home. It’s strange how easy it is to sacrifice today for a tomorrow that might not look anything like we imagined. I’ve found that appreciating life doesn’t mean ignoring problems; it means not letting those problems take every good moment away. Small things like a conversation or a walk can matter more than we realize.
